packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 18 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this item. I opened only PROMPT.md and the 20 image files of this packet. I did nothing beyond the rules. I make no attempt to identify work or author.

LANGUAGE: not Latin. The text is a Netherlandic vernacular (Middle Dutch; spellings such as "hij", "zij(n)", "ghenouchte", "heymelic", "up dat", "zo salmene").

1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image only)

Four overviews: image-001.jpg, image-006.jpg, image-011.jpg, image-016.jpg. Each shows an opened bifolium-shaped piece of paper or parchment with a vertical central fold and two pages side by side, text upright. Each page has ONE column. I call the four views faces 1-4 and the pages "left" and "right" as seen. Tiles: 002-005 belong to face 1, 007-010 to face 2, 012-015 to face 3, 017-020 to face 4.

Observations:
- Small pages, 18-21 lines per page as preserved. On faces 1 and 2 the lower lines are covered by repair tissue and partly lost; on faces 3 and 4 the page ends cleanly after 18-21 lines with blank space below, and the lower edge is ragged.
- No running titles, no rubricated headings, no enlarged initials. Red pilcrows (image-004, -005, -008, -009, -010, -020), red strokes on capitals (D, E, W, M, A, U), and extensive red underlining of whole passages of several lines.
- No interlinear gloss. Two small interlinear/marginal corrections: image-007.jpg l.7-8 (small letters written under the end of "mense"), and image-013.jpg l.9 (red insertion mark after "mense" with a small "a" in the right margin).
- Modern pencil marks: "5"(?) at top right of face 2 (image-008.jpg) and "f3-36"(?) at the top of face 3 (image-013.jpg); not read with confidence.
- Face 4 carries a heavy offset of a much larger formal script running at 90 degrees to the text (vertical bands of large black letters), plus a grey-blue offset along the fold. It obscures parts of most lines there. I did not try to read the offset.
- A horizontal fold crosses each page (around l.3-4 on faces 3-4, around l.16-17 on faces 1-2).

Tentative interpretation (not observation): the red-underlined passages look like lemmata of a base text (they contain rules in the form "if he ... then one shall ..."), each followed by un-underlined exposition introduced by "Daer omme seit hij ...". I keep the two kinds of text marked below as [UL] (underlined) and plain.

Page order is not determined from the images. Several pages begin and end mid-sentence, and I did not find two pages whose text visibly runs on into each other within one face, which suggests the two halves of each face are not consecutive pages.

2. SPANS SELECTED
All eight pages were read, as fully as the script allows. Unread or only partly read: the tissue-covered bottom lines of faces 1 and 2, and words under the offset on face 4.

Line numbers are counted from the top of the named tile. Where a line is visible in two overlapping tiles I give it once and note the overlap.
